title: AI-powered identity threat defense: How Okta is redefining trust in the era of identity fabric and AI agents
summary: Discover how Okta’s identity security fabric protects both human users and AI agents from identity threats with unified governance, adaptive access, and agent-aware security.
body_markdown:
Key takeaways


Okta secures AI agents by treating them as first-class identities within the identity security fabric and applying the same governance, monitoring, and access controls as for human users.


Cross App Access (XAA) standardizes agent-to-app security by moving authentication to the identity layer, eliminating ad hoc credentials and ensuring auditable, policy-driven access.


Just-in-time, least-privilege access minimizes risk by granting AI agents only the permissions they need, only when they need them, and revoking access after use.


Continuous behavioral monitoring detects threats in real time, enabling automated responses, such as access revocation, when AI agents exhibit suspicious behavior.


Unified identity governance ensures compliance readiness by providing comprehensive audit trails and lifecycle management for all human and non-human identities.


Organizations across the globe are prioritizing the management of[non-human identities (NHIs)](https://www.okta.com/identity-101/what-are-non-human-identities/) —machine-based credentials like API keys and service accounts. The identity surface of organizations is growing rapidly as they embrace generative AI, automation tools, and AI agents. Because service accounts, APIs, bots, and AI agents are now part of the digital workforce, securing only human users is no longer sufficient. These NHIs promise greater efficiency and productivity, but they also introduce new attack surfaces. Without proper[governance](https://www.okta.com/products/identity-governance/) , credential hygiene, continuous monitoring, and[lifecycle management](https://www.okta.com/products/lifecycle-management/) , these unmanaged identities can pose serious security risks.


That's where the[identity security fabric](https://www.okta.com/solutions/identity-security-fabric/) emerges as a fundamental solution. **The identity security fabric is a unified framework that provides consistent security posture, governance, and visibility for every identity—human or machine** . Okta is redefining trust by embedding AI agent security within this secure identity fabric, enabling enterprises to harness the power of AI safely and responsibly.


In this post, we examine how Okta integrates AI agents into the identity security fabric to deliver AI-powered identity threat defense, helping enterprises successfully deploy AI without jeopardizing trust.


## Why are non-human identities the primary security risk for AI adoption?


Organizations today employ more than just people:


- Automation tools, shared accounts, and service accounts
- OAuth tokens, API keys, and access tokens
- AI agents (autonomous bots, automation bots, and generative AI assistants)


According to industry research, non-human identities now outnumber human identities by a ratio of 45:1 in typical enterprise environments, and this gap is expected to widen as AI agent adoption accelerates. Okta predicts that the number of NHIs will increase dramatically in the coming years, particularly as AI agents are deployed more frequently. Yet many of these identities remain unmanaged; they often lack[multi-factor authentication (MFA)](https://www.okta.com/products/adaptive-multi-factor-authentication/) , are non-federated, use static credentials, and have excessive privileges.


Compromised non-human identities can provide persistent, high-privilege access that frequently goes undetected, creating a large blind spot in traditional identity management and an attractive attack surface.


Therefore, organizations need a new paradigm that treats each identity as a first-class entity within a single security architecture.


## What is an identity security fabric, and how does it protect machine access?


An[identity security fabric](https://www.okta.com/identity-101/identity-fabric-the-future-of-identity-and-access-management/) is more than just a concept; it's a comprehensive, multilayered architecture that combines threat detection, privileged access,[identity governance](https://www.okta.com/products/identity-governance/) , and more across all identity types (human, machine, and AI agents) and hybrid infrastructure.


Unlike fragmented point solutions that create security gaps, an identity security fabric weaves identity capabilities together as a unified security layer, providing centralized control where traditional identity and access management (IAM) approaches fall short.


### Key benefits of an identity security fabric:


Benefit Description Use case


**Unified visibility and control** Eliminates silos by managing all identities in a single control plane Consolidating human, machine, and AI agent identities across hybrid environments


**Consistent governance at scale** Applies the same lifecycle policies ([automated provisioning](https://www.okta.com/identity-101/automated-provisioning/) , de-provisioning, access review,[entitlement management](https://www.okta.com/identity-101/entitlement-management-identity-governance-explained/) ) to all identities, including service accounts, bots, and AI agents Applying uniform access policies to thousands of service accounts and AI agents


**Adaptive, risk-aware access** Evaluates access decisions based on context, least-privilege enforcement, and real-time risk assessment Dynamically adjusting AI agent permissions based on behavioral signals


**Continuous threat monitoring and response** Employs ongoing[identity threat protection](https://www.okta.com/products/identity-threat-protection/) , including behavioral analytics and anomaly detection, to identify and address threats caused by NHIs Detecting and responding to compromised service accounts in real time


In simple terms, an identity security fabric converts identity from a static, credential-based concept into a dynamic, continuously monitored security boundary, which is crucial when AI agents act independently at machine speed.


## How does Okta secure AI agents across the identity lifecycle?


Okta expands its platform to secure AI agents and other non-human identities through the following capabilities:


### Discover and categorize every identity


Okta identifies and classifies all non-human identities—including service accounts, API keys, AI agents, and orphaned credentials—using[Identity Security Posture Management](https://www.okta.com/products/identity-security-posture-management/) . This enables security teams to see what they have and where risks lie by classifying each identity with metadata such as owner, risk level, and usage trends.


### Identity registry and unified directory


All identities, human and non-human, are brought into a[single registry under uniform control](https://www.okta.com/identity-101/establishing-directory-policies/) , ensuring each identity has an official record with ownership, attributes, and governance policies.


### Privileged access: Least-privilege and just-in-time access


In contrast to broad or permanent credentials, Okta enables fine-grained, least-privilege access control for AI agents and non-human identities. Access can be narrowly scoped, granted only when necessary, and revoked after use. This just-in-time access significantly limits the blast radius of potential security breaches.


### Secure agent-to-app interactions: Cross App Access (XAA)


[Cross App Access](https://www.okta.com/solutions/cross-app-access/) (XAA) secures agent-driven communications by moving authentication and authorization to the identity layer, ensuring every agent's access is centrally regulated and auditable.


This standardization enables developers to create "fabric-ready" AI agents that connect to the identity fabric by default, ensuring consistent security across the entire organization.


### Identity protection: Governance, monitoring, and threat detection


Okta goes beyond provisioning and access controls; it continuously monitors identity activity, employs behavioral analytics to detect abnormalities, logs all actions, and provides comprehensive governance.


If an AI agent behaves suspiciously, Okta can initiate rapid automated responses, such as revoking access, alerting security teams, or isolating the identity to prevent potential threats.


### Compliance, auditability, and lifecycle management


Unified identity governance enables enterprises to manage audit trails and access certificates for all identities, supporting compliance frameworks (such as SOC 2 and ISO 27001) and AI-related legal obligations.


## What are the key enterprise benefits of identity-centric AI security?


Okta provides organizations with a roadmap for implementing AI and automation while maintaining security and compliance by embedding AI agent security within a secure identity fabric. The key benefits include:


- **Visibility into hidden risks:** Many organizations have no idea how many service accounts, bots, or AI agents are in use. Okta helps uncover these blind spots.
- **Decreased attack surface:** Just-in-time provisioning and least-privilege access prevent agents from gaining unnecessary access, reducing risk.
- **Standardized, scalable security:** Open protocols like XAA and consistent governance eliminate a fragmented patchwork, creating consistent security across apps, APIs, clouds, and on-premises environments.
- **Operational efficiency with safety:** Okta manages the identity lifecycle, governance, and auditability, allowing automation and AI to thrive without manual overhead.
- **Audit-ready and regulation-ready posture:** Unified identity logging and governance help meet compliance requirements and prepare for future AI-specific regulations.


Identity is the foundation of trust for both humans and machines, enabling the confident adoption of AI. As AI agents become an integral part of enterprise workflows, securing non-human identities with the same rigor as human identities is essential.


## Ready to lock down your AI identity security?


If you're thinking about building or expanding an AI-driven enterprise, embracing an[identity security fabric](https://www.okta.com/solutions/identity-security-fabric/) is more than just a best practice; it's the defense architecture that transforms AI-driven risk into managed trust.


Okta turns identity into a centralized security control layer that protects everyone and everything, including employees, service accounts, automation tools, API keys, and AI agents. Okta enables enterprises to harness the power of AI safely and responsibly by providing unified visibility, least-privilege access, standardized protocols, continuous monitoring, and audit-ready governance.


Don’t let siloed tools and blind spots compromise your security posture. See firsthand how a unified identity security fabric eliminates risk and agent access at scale.[Watch the Identity Security Fabric demo](https://www.okta.com/resources/demos/identity-security-fabric/) to discover how to protect your enterprise against modern AI-driven threats.


## Frequently asked questions


###

It combines threat detection, privileged access, and identity governance into a single, multi-layered architecture.


###


AI agents act autonomously at machine speed, often with elevated privileges across multiple systems. Without proper identity security, they create blind spots that attackers can exploit for persistent, undetected access. An identity security fabric ensures AI agents are governed, monitored, and secured like any other identity.
